claims: Ostara is a modern Pagan and Wiccan holiday.
Ostara is celebrated on the spring equinox.
The spring equinox is around March 20–21 in the Northern Hemisphere.
Ostara marks the first day of spring.
Ostara is named after the Germanic goddess Eostre (or Ostara).
The Germanic goddess Eostre (or Ostara) is associated with spring, dawn, and fertility.
Ostara is one of the eight Sabbats in the Wiccan Wheel of the Year.
Ostara marks the point when day and night are of equal length.
Symbols of Ostara include spring flowers.

Many modern Easter traditions, including the Easter Bunny and egg decorating, are thought to be derived from the ancient customs and mythology surrounding Eostre and the celebration of spring's arrival.
